sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive leadership dominates the tape as Consumer Defensive and Healthcare post elite momentum scores above 0.90, while cyclical sectors like Technology, Industrials, and Materials lose ground.

Market breadth remains exceptionally narrow, with only 2 of 11 sectors posting all-green profiles across all tracked timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, YTD). Leadership is firmly anchored in low-beta groups, with Consumer Defensive and Healthcare consistently holding top-three ranks across 1-, 3-, and 6-month periods. Meanwhile, Energy holds the top YTD rank (rank 1) with moderate momentum (0.567), but lacks the sustained multi-period breadth seen in the defensive leaders.

Short-term rotation favored rate-sensitive and financial names, as Real Estate, Financials, and Utilities each ticked up +1 spot over the last five sessions. Conversely, economically sensitive growth and cyclical groups are fading: Technology, Industrials, and Basic Materials all slipped -1 spot in five-day rank, with Communication Services (0.167) and Basic Materials (0.183) sinking to the bottom of the momentum rankings.

## Strength
- **Narrow All-Green Breadth:** Only 2 of 11 sectors are green across all horizons (week, month, quarter, half, YTD): Consumer Defensive (momentum 0.933) and Healthcare (momentum 0.900).
- **Sustained Leadership:** Consumer Defensive and Healthcare represent the only sectors demonstrating sustained top-3 rankings across 1-, 3-, and 6-month evaluations.
- **Top Absolute Rank:** Energy maintains the #1 YTD rank, carrying a 0.567 momentum score, though it sits behind Consumer Defensive (rank 2) and Healthcare (rank 3) in overall momentum.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Five-Day Rank Gainers:** Real Estate (+1 spot to rank 4, momentum 0.600), Financials (+1 spot to rank 6, momentum 0.517), and Utilities (+1 spot to rank 8, momentum 0.467) showed the strongest short-term rank improvements.
- **Five-Day Rank Losers:** Technology (-1 spot to rank 5, momentum 0.300), Industrials (-1 spot to rank 7, momentum 0.350), and Basic Materials (-1 spot to rank 9, momentum 0.183) saw the steepest five-session declines.
- **Severe Momentum Laggards:** Communication Services sits at the bottom of the board across the board, occupying rank 11 with a market-low momentum score of 0.167.

## Divergences
- **Energy Rank vs. Momentum Disconnect:** Despite holding the #1 YTD rank, Energy's momentum score (0.567) trails significantly behind rank 2 Consumer Defensive (0.933) and rank 3 Healthcare (0.900).
- **Growth Sector Deterioration:** Technology retains a mid-tier YTD position (rank 5) despite carrying an anemic momentum score of 0.300 and falling -1 spot over the last week.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensives and select consumer niches maintain market leadership, while retail and housing-related groups mount short-term rallies as metals and mining sharply deteriorate.

Leadership remains concentrated in non-cyclical and consumer staples pockets, with 15 of 144 groups holding all-green breadth across all monitored timeframes. Discount Stores (momentum 0.917) and Furnishings, Fixtures & Appliances (momentum 0.889) anchor this strength alongside steady bids in Insurance (Reinsurance, Brokers, and Property & Casualty) and Drug Manufacturers - General (momentum 0.865). 

A pronounced short-term rotation is lifting consumer discretionary and retail names, highlighted by sharp five-day rank jumps in Department Stores (+26 spots to rank 66) and Apparel Retail (+20 spots to rank 94). Conversely, basic materials and mining are unraveling rapidly, driven by severe drops in Copper (-43 spots to rank 98), Gold (-19 spots to rank 120), and Silver (-16 spots to rank 132), leaving commodity spaces among the weakest performers in the market.

## Strength
- **Narrow all-green breadth:** Only 15 of 144 groups remain positive across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD windows, led by Discount Stores (0.917 momentum) and Insurance - Reinsurance (0.881 momentum).
- **Persistent defensive positioning:** Drug Manufacturers - General (0.865 momentum, rank 14), Insurance Brokers (0.79 momentum), and Insurance - Property & Casualty (0.79 momentum) are among the few groups holding sustained top-36 rank strength over 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
- **Top momentum clusters:** Absolute momentum leaders are heavily concentrated in Discount Stores (0.917), Furnishings, Fixtures & Appliances (0.889), Insurance - Reinsurance (0.881), Drug Manufacturers - General (0.865), and Consumer Electronics (0.859, rank 7).

## Movers & Momentum
- **Retail rebound:** Department Stores led all five-day gainers, leaping +26 spots to rank 66 (0.70 momentum), followed by Apparel Retail jumping +20 spots to rank 94 (0.55 momentum) and Apparel Manufacturing gaining +17 spots to rank 57 (0.74 momentum).
- **Metals unwind:** Severe five-day drops hit Copper (-43 spots to rank 98, 0.21 momentum), Other Industrial Metals & Mining (-20 spots to rank 102, 0.19 momentum), Gold (-19 spots to rank 120, 0.18 momentum), and Silver (-16 spots to rank 132, 0.12 momentum).
- **Absolute laggards:** Uranium (0.021 momentum, rank 142), Solar (0.028 momentum, rank 143), Other Precious Metals & Mining (0.033 momentum, rank 141), and Gambling (0.070 momentum, rank 144) sit at the absolute bottom of momentum rankings.

## Divergences
- **Early-stage building improvements:** Building Products & Equipment (+7 spots in 5d, 0.44 momentum), Building Materials (+6 spots, 0.49 momentum), and Real Estate Services (+6 spots, 0.47 momentum) are jumping in rank despite sub-0.50 momentum profiles.
- **Slipping high-momentum names:** Lodging (momentum 0.81, rank -1 in 5d), Insurance - Diversified (momentum 0.76, rank -1 in 5d), Medical Care Facilities (momentum 0.69, rank -2 in 5d), and Industrial Distribution (momentum 0.62, rank -5 in 5d) are exhibiting early fatigue as short-term rank drifts lower despite solid overall momentum.
